body:
## Problem / why
The current integration baseline is red before BI-PF-1567 changes are considered. Precheck reports seven new open items without api_impact/epic/detailed AC (BI-PF-1603..BI-PF-1609), 112 backlog-context problems across open items, and a completed BI-PF-1566 that lacks Gate 2/Gate 2.5 and completion trail evidence. This blocks every delivery branch, including otherwise green work.

## Goal & value
Restore a trustworthy baseline so feature branches can merge on their own merits, and close the authority/bookkeeping drift that made completed work look invalid.

## In scope
- Repair BI-PF-1603 through BI-PF-1609: epic, context, detailed AC, api_impact with reason/routes.
- Repair open product_forge backlog context until backlog-context passes.
- Reconcile DB/file projections and generated docs under both PF_BACKLOG_DB=on and off.
- Re-run precheck fast and prove the baseline is green.

## Out of scope
- BI-PF-1567 memory-orchestrator implementation.
- New product features or schema changes.
- Reopening rejected BI-PF-1538.

## Closure note
The BI-PF-1566/1550 completion failures were false transitions caused by a stale local develop ref plus our own inspection edits; no HIL Gate 2 approval was fabricated. Repairing the local develop ref restored zero-transition checks.

verification: Objective achieved: Restore a trustworthy baseline so feature branches can merge on their own merits, and close the authority/bookkeeping drift that made completed work look invalid.

NIT: 'affected_components: Not specified' in Gate-1 context despite design_pack naming concrete components.
operation_matrix and config_contract (PF_BACKLOG_DB) appear in functional_spec but are never referenced by any FR/control in this item's scope.
MAJOR: Design covers only the rejected-skip predicate; no FR, control, or test addresses acceptance criteria 1-3 (BI-PF-1603..1609 disposition, backlog-context zero-problem gate, precheck green on develop) or criterion 4 (PF_BACKLOG_DB on/off projection consistency), so the item's acceptance contract is unmet by the approved design.

'All three predicates agree' is an stated invariant, yet the change adds the status set independently in three files (design_pack/functional_spec/spec_pack) with no shared predicate module — structural drift risk against the invariant.

Status semantics are inconsistent: FR edge cases and C-3 include 'cancelled'/'won't_do', but decisions, invariants, and failure_matrix only name 'rejected/cancelled'; 'won't_do' behavior is undefined, leaving the skip set ambiguous.
Design does not embed or reference latest Gate 1.5 findings/dispositions or the guardrail checklist answers (CL-006/CL-008), so Gate 1 approval evidence is incomplete.
MINOR: FR inputs list 'item.created_at' but no requirement, control, or edge case defines any rule using it — dead input in the contract.
Evidence SHAs are inconsistent: functional_spec 'functional_sha' 2e1047808fdb vs all ac_evidence/controls 'candidate_sha' bc5a6145 — traceability unclear (CL-015 intent).
No explicit test named for 'cancelled'/'won't_do' despite appearing in edge_cases; coverage claim rests on inferred test content.
Rollback is 'revert patch' only; no statement that the revert restores enforcement for previously skipped items (acceptable for read-only tooling but unverified).
security_threat_model declared APPLICABLE for a read-only status predicate; over-declared scope for a N/A-class concern.
SUMMARY: Design is coherent and low-risk for the rejected-skip predicate itself (read-only, fail-closed on unknown, testable, Python tooling within language rule), but it only addresses one of four acceptance criteria and leaves three remediation obligations with no coverage.

Top risks: untested acceptance criteria (backlog-context, precheck-on-develop, DB/file projection parity), triplicated predicate violating its own agreement invariant, and undefined 'won't_do' skip semantics.
Recommend Gate 1.5 hold until AC-to-FR traceability for criteria 1-4 is added or the remaining criteria are split into separately gated items.

NIT: Test file `test_gates_skip_rejected.py` under-describes coverage of cancelled/won't-do/live/unknown statuses.
`functional_sha` (a38a9e99c9fb) still differs from all `candidate_sha` (bc5a6145) despite the prior disposition claiming this traceability item was ACTIONED.
MAJOR: AC-4 ("precheck fast tier passes with rejected baseline items present and fails closed for unknown statuses") has no corresponding control, coverage entry, or test: test_matrix is entirely unit pytest against one file, so the approved design cannot evidence this end-to-end AC.

AC-1's "one shared predicate" is asserted but no test or static check proves the three gates actually import `gate_status.should_skip` rather than keeping local copies; behavioral tests alone permit silent re-forking of the terminal set.
MINOR: Status literals remain inconsistent across artifacts: AC says `won-t-do`/`wont-do`, FR edge_cases say `won't_do`/`wont_do`, failure_matrix says `won-t_do`/`wont_do`; an exact-match predicate using the wrong literal would fail closed on a supposedly terminal item.
`controls` and `implementation_controls` are byte-identical duplicated blocks — guaranteed drift as edits land in one and not the other.

Entrypoint contradiction: coverage/entrypoint lists `scripts/dev/gate_status.py:should_skip` while `runtime_contract.entrypoint` lists `scripts/dev/design_pack.py:should_enforce`; the single source of truth is ambiguous.

Skips are not observable: gate output reports only a checked count with no skipped-count or skip-reason, so diagnosing why an item was skipped requires reading code (guardrail 10 minimum diagnostics).
Control kinds are mislabeled (C-2 `kind: config`, C-3 `kind: security` for pure status predicates), misrouting review/security scoping for a tooling-only change.
SUMMARY: Sound approach overall: shared pure predicate, fail-closed unknown handling, tooling-only Python (language rule compliant), and no data/API/security surface.
Top risks: AC-4 lacks any precheck-level evidence in the approved controls/tests, and the shared-predicate invariant is asserted rather than structurally enforced.
Residual artifact-hygiene issues (literal mismatches, duplicated control blocks, contradictory entrypoints) undermine the traceability the design is meant to restore.

NIT: CL-008 guardrail checklist items 2/3/5/8/9 are answered only implicitly (security_note, rls_tenant: "N/A"); an explicit guardrail-answers block in the design would make Gate 1.5 verification mechanical.
All four FRs share one test file and one evidence doc, so traceability rows are indistinguishable; add per-FR test node-ids.
MAJOR: Disposition integrity: prior findings marked ACTIONED are unchanged in artifacts — `controls`/`implementation_controls` still byte-identical, `runtime_contract.entrypoint` still `design_pack.py:should_enforce` vs `coverage.entrypoint` `gate_status.py:should_skip`, and `functional_sha` (46397b51a002) ≠ `candidate_sha` (bc5a6145); Gate-1.5 evidence is unreliable (CL-006).

Guardrail 10 unmet: `observability_detail.gate_output` remains "checked count" with no skipped-count or skip reason, so a silently skipped item is undiagnosable from gate output; the ACTIONED disposition does not hold.

AC-3 lacks an explicit coverage matrix: design `test_matrix` maps each AC to one aggregate pytest invocation with no terminal-status × gate (4 statuses × 3 gates) enumeration, so per-gate, per-status completeness is asserted rather than evidenced.
MINOR: Positive control/test name `test_rejected_status_skips_design_and_spec_gates` names only two gates; AC-1 requires functional-spec too — add an explicit functional_spec assertion or gate-parametrized test name.
Rollback is only "revert the change"; guardrail 6 expects a fail-able check that revert restores enforcement (no post-revert test step defined).
`failure_matrix` lists only `in_progress` as the live case while AC-2 says "live statuses" plural; enumerate the representative live set (e.g. backlog, in_review) in design evidence.
Control kinds remain odd for tooling predicates (`C-3 kind: security`, `C-2 kind: config`), which misroutes review scope even after the prior disposition.
SUMMARY: Sound approach: shared `gate_status.should_skip` predicate with fail-closed unknown handling satisfies the core AC intent and the language rule (tooling Python).

Top risks: several prior ACTIONED dispositions are not reflected in the current artifacts, undermining Gate-1.5 trust; skip decisions remain unobservable; AC-3's status×gate coverage is asserted, not evidenced.
Recommend re-verifying dispositions against the actual design doc before Gate 1.5 sign-off.

NIT: `failure_taxonomy` enumerates only `predicate exception, unknown status, rejected skip`, omitting the other three terminal statuses named in AC-1.
`functional_spec.status` and `spec_pack.status` remain `draft` while design asserts `candidate_sha`-pinned evidence; finalizing status would make Gate 1.5 verification mechanical.
MAJOR: AC-4 proof mechanism unspecified: no described spy/monkeypatch/source assertion showing all three gates actually invoke `gate_status.should_skip`; behavioral parity tests cannot prove call-site wiring, so AC-4 may be unmeetable with the listed tests.

Disposition-wrong re-report: prior ACTIONED dispositions are not reflected in the provided design — `controls`/`implementation_controls` still byte-identical, `observability_detail.gate_output` still "checked count" (no skip count/reason), `test_matrix` still one aggregate pytest per AC.

Traceability misalignment: AC-3 (terminal-status × gate regression) binds to FR-3 ("Apply predicate in functional/spec pack") and C-3 (`gate_status.py:should_skip`), while FR-4 is the regression FR — AC↔FR↔control mapping is internally inconsistent for Gate 2 evidence.
MINOR: AC-3 evidence lacks a named test covering `cancelled`/`won't_do`/`wont_do`; only `rejected` appears in proof_plan/positive-test names, so per-status completeness is asserted, not evidenced.
`ac_evidence.candidate_sha` (bc5a6145) differs from `functional_spec.functional_sha` (46397b51a002) with no stated relationship; CL-015 pinning is ambiguous.
`proof_plan.green_evidence` is prose ("after fix rejected items are skipped") rather than a runnable check with output/SHA.
`operation_matrix.error` misuses the error column for normal behavior ("unknown remains enforced"), which will misroute failure triage.
SUMMARY: Sound, narrowly scoped tooling change with a single shared fail-closed predicate and explicit terminal set — right direction and language-rule compliant.

Top risks: AC-4 cannot be proven by the specified behavioral tests, AC↔FR↔control traceability is inconsistent, and prior ACTIONED dispositions are not visible in the supplied design artifacts (observability of skips and per-status/per-gate coverage evidence still missing).
Recommend Gate 1.5 hold until call-site proof, per-status × gate evidence, and skip observability are concretely reflected in the design.

functional_spec.outcome: Rejected terminal items no longer force design/spec artifacts while live and unknown statuses remain enforced.
open_questions: None. Terminal statuses are exactly rejected, cancelled, won't_do, and wont_do.

acceptance_criteria: Terminal statuses rejected, cancelled, won't_do, and wont_do are skipped by design-pack, functional-spec, and spec-pack enforcement through one shared predicate.
Live statuses and unknown statuses remain enforced exactly as before, with no broad skip.
A regression test covers every terminal skip status plus live and unknown statuses across all three gates.
A regression test proves all three gates call the shared gate_status.should_skip predicate and that the terminal status set is explicit.
